rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualifier about God's will rebuts the Murji'a: forgiveness for sins below shirk is for some sinners, not automatically every believer.
rows.anchor: لمن يشاء راد على المرجئة، إذ مدلوله أن غفران ما دون الشرك إنما هو لقوم دون قوم

rows.speaker: المعتزلة والمرجئة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila and Murji'a tried to force the verse into their doctrines through interpretations Abu Hayyan calls invalid and contrary to its meaning.
rows.anchor: وقد رامت المعتزلة والمرجئة رد هذه الآية إلى مقالاتهما بتأويلات لا تصح

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes both clauses as governed by God's will: shirk is not forgiven for someone who dies unrepentant, while lesser sins may be forgiven for a repentant person.
rows.anchor: الوجه أن يكون الفعل المنفي والمثبت جميعا موجهين إلى قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan asks where it is established that forgiveness of major sins below shirk requires repentance; general texts can be qualified, and Ibn Abbas limits the intentional-murder threat to one who deems murder lawful.
rows.anchor: وإنما يستدلون بعمومات تحتمل التخصيص، كاستدلالهم بقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching the prepositional phrase to both verbs is invalid; restricting the first verb by God's will as well is an imposed interpretation.
rows.anchor: إن عنى أن الجار يتعلق بالفعلين، فلا يصح ذلك.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: On al-Zamakhshari's reading, the subject of “wills” is the person: God does not forgive the unrepentant idolater but may forgive a repentant sinner below shirk.
rows.anchor: والذي يفهم من كلامه أن الضمير الفاعل في قوله: يشاء عائد على من، لا على الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan reads the first clause without a will-condition and takes God as the subject of “wills” in the second, leaving great hope for sinners below shirk even if they die unrepentant.
rows.anchor: والذي يدل عليه ظاهر الكلام أنه لا قيد في الفعل الأول بالمشيئة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats everlasting residence as a long stay rather than endless duration; Abu Hayyan rejects this in the surrounding argument.
rows.anchor: وقال: الخلود يراد به المكث الطويل لا الديمومة لا إلى نهاية

words: ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says they once testified that a person who died with a major sin belonged to Hell, but stopped making such judgments after this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر: كنا على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: Ubadah reports that whoever commits one of the earlier-mentioned sins and is concealed by God is left to God's decision: He may pardon or punish.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث عبادة بن الصامت في آخره «ومن أصاب شيئا من ذلك

words: لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك لمن يشاء
rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali and other Companions are reported to have said that no Qur'an verse was more beloved to them than this one.
rows.anchor: ويروى عن علي وغيره من الصحابة: ما في القرآن آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates Jews count as polytheists in religious usage: otherwise they would be distinct from polytheists and receive the promised forgiveness; the preceding threat targets Jews.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل على أن اليهودي يسمى مشركا في عرف الشرع،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: References distinguishing Jews from polytheists do so linguistically, while the categories coincide in religious usage.
rows.anchor: فالمغايرة وقعت بحسب المفهوم اللغوي، والاتحاد بحسب المفهوم الشرعي.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says every disbeliever is a polytheist because denying a prophet's revelation assigns to someone besides God what belongs only to God.
rows.anchor: وقد قال الزجاج: كل كافر مشرك، لأنه إذا كفر مثلا بنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says conversion removes the earlier description of disbelief by consensus and cites the prophetic statement that Islam erases what came before.
rows.anchor: لأن الإيمان يزيل عنه إطلاق الوصف بما تقدمه من الكفر بإجماع،

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Asked which sin is greatest, the Prophet answered that it is setting up a rival for God who created the person.
rows.anchor: وسئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أي الذنب أعظم؟ قال:

words: ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم
rows.speaker: الجمهور والحسن وابن زيد
rows.claim: The majority identify those who praise themselves as Jews; al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd identify them as Christians.
rows.anchor: قال الجمهور: هم اليهود. وقال الحسن وابن زيد: هم النصارى.

words: ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم
rows.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
rows.claim: They report that Marhab ibn Zayd, Bahri ibn Amr, and other Jews brought children to Muhammad and asked whether they were sinful; after he said no, they claimed their own sins were similarly erased, prompting the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك والسدي في آخرين: أتى مرحب بن زيد

words: ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they claimed to be God's sons and beloved ones.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو قولهم: نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه.

words: ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم
rows.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد وأبو مالك
rows.claim: They say the Jews presented prepubescent children as prayer leaders, claiming the sinless children would secure forgiveness for the adults praying behind them.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة، ومجاهد، وأبو مالك: كانوا يقدمون الصبيان

words: ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم
rows.speaker: قتادة والحسن
rows.claim: They explain the self-praise as claims that Jews or Christians are God's beloved children and that only Jews or Christians enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة والحسن: هو قولهم: نحن أبناء الله وأحباؤه

words: ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse censures people who verbally praise themselves by claiming exceptional obedience, piety, and nearness to God.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على الغض ممن يزكي نفسه بلسانه

words: ألم تر إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم
rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari cites the Prophet's assertion that he was trustworthy in heaven and earth, made when hypocrites accused him of unfair distribution; God's attestation differs from self-praise or uninformed praise.
rows.anchor: شهد لنفسه أو شهد له من لا يعلم. قاله الزمخشري

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes purification by deeds that display virtue from speech that reports and praises virtue.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب ما ملخصه: التزكية ضربان: بالفعل

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says a person is forbidden to purify himself or another except in a specified circumstance, because only God knows a person's inner state.
rows.anchor: وحظر أن يزكي الإنسان نفسه، بل أن يزكي غيره، إلا على وجه مخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Rather” shifts away from their self-praise because they are not qualified to certify themselves.
rows.anchor: بل: إضراب عن تزكيتهم أنفسهم، إذ ليسوا أهلا لذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is the authoritative purifier because He knows hidden realities; He purifies whomever He chooses by making that person pure and describing them as purified.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن المزكي هو الله تعالى، وأنه تعالى هو المعتد بتزكيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A thread” denotes a tiny amount, as in the statement that God does not wrong an atom's weight; if He wrongs no tiny amount, He will wrong nothing greater.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أقل شيء كقوله: إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with the atom's weight reinforces the assurance that God wrongs nothing.
rows.anchor: كقوله: إن الله لا يظلم مثقال ذرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to those praising themselves or, by sense, to the chosen person; Abu Hayyan prefers the latter as nearest, while Ibn Atiyya gives the broader option of both groups mentioned.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا أن يعود الضمير في: ولا يظلمون، إلى الذين يزكون أنفسهم

rows.speaker: عمر ومجاهد والشعبي
rows.claim: Umar, Mujahid, and al-Sha'bi identify jibt as sorcery.
rows.anchor: الجبت السحر قاله: عمر، ومجاهد، والشعبي.

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam identifies taghut as Satan.
rows.anchor: والطاغوت الشيطان قاله: زيد بن أسلم.

rows.speaker: رفيع وابن جبير
rows.claim: Rafi' and Ibn Jubayr say jibt is a sorcerer and taghut is a soothsayer.
rows.anchor: الجبت الساحر، والطاغوت الكاهن، قاله: رفيع وابن جبير.

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: In another view, Ibn Jubayr defines jibt as a soothsayer and taghut as Satan.
rows.anchor: الجبت الكاهن، والطاغوت الشيطان، قاله: ابن جبير أيضا.

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin says jibt means a soothsayer and taghut a sorcerer.
rows.anchor: الجبت الكاهن، والطاغوت الساحر، قاله: ابن سيرين.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies jibt as Satan and taghut as a soothsayer.
rows.anchor: الجبت الشيطان، والطاغوت الكاهن قاله: قتادة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view identifies jibt as Ka'b and taghut as Satan appearing in human form.
rows.anchor: الجبت كعب، والطاغوت الشيطان كان في صورة إنسان،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says jibt is idols and everything worshipped besides God, while taghut is Satan.
rows.anchor: أو الجبت الأصنام وكل ما عبد من دون الله، والطاغوت الشيطان قاله: الزمخشري.

rows.speaker: الزجاج وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Qutayba define both terms as any object of worship besides God, whether stone, image, or Satan.
rows.anchor: أو الجبت والطاغوت كل معبود من دون الله من حجر، أو صورة، أو شيطان قاله: الزجاج، وابن قتيبة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Other reports from Ibn Abbas define jibt as idols, Ka'b al-Ashraf, a soothsayer, or translators before idols, with attributions to al-Dahhak, al-Farra', al-Layth, al-Awfi, and Ikrima.
rows.anchor: أو الأصنام رواه عطية عن ابن عباس، وبه قال الضحاك، والفراء،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is also cited for defining jibt as Ka'b al-Ashraf; reports come through al-Dahhak and al-Layth from Mujahid.
rows.anchor: أو كعب بن الأشرف. رواه الضحاك، عن ابن عباس. وليث، عن مجاهد.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mukahul, Ibn Sirin, and Ikrima are associated with defining jibt as a soothsayer.
rows.anchor: وبه قال: مكحول، وابن سيرين.

rows.speaker: ابن جبير وقتادة والسدي وأبو العالية وابن زيد
rows.claim: Jibt is also reported as Satan by Ibn Jubayr, Qatada, and al-Suddi, or as a sorcerer by Abu al-Aliya and Ibn Zayd.
rows.anchor: أو الشيطان قاله: ابن جبير في رواية، وقتادة والسدي أو الساحر قاله: أبو العالية وابن زيد.

rows.speaker: أبو بشر عن ابن جبير
rows.claim: A report says jibt means sorcerer in Ethiopian, while taghut means Satan.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو بشر عن ابن جبير قال: الجبت الساحر بلسان الحبشة

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik gives both terms the broad sense of anything worshipped besides God; some say the words are synonymous, but the majority say they refer to two things.
rows.anchor: أو كل ما عبد من دون الله قاله: مالك. وقال قوم: الجبت والطاغوت مترادفان

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Abu Dawud transmits the Prophet's statement that divination by lines, omens, and augury are forms of jibt; Abu Hayyan explains line-divination and augury.
rows.anchor: خرج أبو داود في سننه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «الطرق والطيرة والعيافة من الجبت»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the terms mean idols, belief means affirming their divinity and worship beside God; if they mean leaders, sorcerers, soothsayers, or Satan, it means obeying and agreeing with them.
rows.anchor: فإن الجبت والطاغوت الأصنام أو ما عبد من دون الله، فالإيمان بهما

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود وعبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas read the phrase without its final nun, applying the grammatical operation of idhan.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن مسعود وعبد الله بن عباس: لا يؤنوا بحذف النون على إعمال اذن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The people” may refer to the Arabs, believers, the Prophet, or Jews and others.
rows.anchor: والناس هنا العرب، أو المؤمنون، أو النبي، أو من اليهود وغيرهم أقوال.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The common explanation, transmitted from Ibn Abbas and shared by many authorities, is that naqir is the tiny mark on the back of a date pit.
rows.anchor: والنقير: النقطة في ظهر النواة رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas instead calls naqir the skin in the middle of a date pit.
rows.anchor: وقيل: القشر يكون في وسط النواة، رواه التميمي عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A report from Mujahid defines naqir as the fiber in the middle of a date pit.
rows.anchor: أو الخيط في وسط النواة، روي عن مجاهد،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya transmits from Ibn Abbas that naqir is a mark made by touching something with the tip of one's thumb.
rows.anchor: أو نقر الرجل الشيء بطرف إبهامه رواه أبو العالية عن ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A report through Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid defines naqir as the seed at the center of a date pit.
rows.anchor: أو حبة النواة التي في وسطها رواه ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد.

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari says fatil, naqir, and qitmir are proverbial for something trivial; using tiny objects in both verse endings creates a fitting parallel.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري: الفتيل والنقير، والقطمير، يضرب مثلا للشيء التافه الحقير،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Am” is a disconnected conjunction equivalent to “rather”; the hamza shifts topics and introduces a rhetorical question of disapproval.
rows.anchor: أم أيضا منقطعة فتقدر ببل. والهمزة فبل: للانتقال من كلام إلى كلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text first rebukes stinginess, which withholds benefit, then envy, which wishes another's God-given good removed; envy is worse, so it comes second.
rows.anchor: أنكر عليهم أولا البخل، ثم ثانيا الحسد. فالبخل منع وصول خير من الإنسان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعكرمة والسدي والضحاك ومقاتل
rows.claim: These authorities identify “the people” as the Prophet and God's favor as prophethood.
rows.anchor: والناس هنا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، والفضل النبوة، قاله: ابن عباس، ومجاهد،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi also interpret God's favor as the Prophet's permission to have many wives.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، والسدي أيضا: والفضل ما أبيح له من النساء.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: They connect the verse to Jews telling Arab pagans that Muhammad claimed a humble mission but cared only about food and women; the question challenges why they envy him rather than Solomon and David.
rows.anchor: وسبب نزول الآية عندهم أن اليهود قالت لكفار العرب: انظروا إلى هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Solomon had seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and David had one hundred wives; in this interpretation, the great dominion includes permission for wives.
rows.anchor: روي أنه كان لسليمان سبعمائة امرأة وثلاثمائة سرية، ولداود مائة امرأة.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the people are the Arabs and God's favor is the messenger: Israel envied the Arabs for receiving a prophet although their ancestors had prophets, scripture, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الناس هنا العرب حسدتها بنو إسرائيل أن كان الرسول منها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported to identify the people as Quraysh.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: نحن الناس يريد قريشا.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the great dominion given to Abraham's family as Solomon's kingdom.
rows.anchor: أي ملك سليمان قاله: ابن عباس.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets the great dominion as prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو النبوة.

rows.speaker: همام بن الحرث وأبو مسلمة وابن زيد
rows.claim: Hammam ibn al-Harith, Abu Maslama, and Ibn Zayd say the great dominion is support from angels.
rows.anchor: وقال همام بن الحرث وأبو مسلمة وابن زيد هو التأييد بالملائكة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the people as Muhammad, Abu Bakr, and Umar; the book as Torah and Gospel, or those plus Psalms; wisdom as prophethood or religious understanding.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الناس هنا الرسول، وأبو بكر، وعمر. والكتاب: التوراة والإنجيل

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
rows.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi interprets wisdom as understanding religion.
rows.anchor: أو الفقه في الدين قاله أبو سليمان الدمشقي.

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi explains the great dominion as combining governance of worldly affairs with religious law.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الملك العظيم هو الجمع بين سياسة الدنيا وشرع الدين ذكره الماوردي.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads God's favor as victory, dominance, and steadily increasing honor.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أم يحسدونهم على ما آتاهم الله من فضله النصرة والغلبة

words: آتينا آل إبراهيم الكتاب والحكمة وآتيناهم ملكا عظيما
rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls the comparison a sound argument: God gave Abraham's family, Muhammad's forebears, scripture and wisdom, so similar favor to Muhammad is unsurprising; Ibn Abbas lists Joseph, David, and Solomon among their kings.
rows.anchor: فقد آتينا إلزام لهم بما عرفوه من إيتاء الله الكتاب والحكمة آل إبراهيم الذين أسلاف محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas includes Joseph, David, and Solomon among the kings of Abraham's family.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: الملك في آل إبراهيم ملك يوسف، وداود، وسليمان،

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says some of Abraham's family believed Abraham and others disbelieved, like the cited division between guided and sinful descendants.
rows.anchor: من آل إبراهيم من آمن بإبراهيم، ومنهم من كفر كقوله: «فمنهم مهتد وكثير منهم فاسقون» قاله السدي:

rows.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل والفراء والجمهور
rows.claim: These authorities say some Jews addressed as people of scripture believed the Qur'an as commanded in the preceding address; this explains why the threatened obliteration did not occur.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد، ومقاتل، والفراء، والجمهور ولذلك ارتفع الطمس ولم يقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views say some Jews believed the favor given to the Prophet or Arabs, the account of Abraham's family, or Muhammad's prophethood, while others denied him.
rows.anchor: أو فمن اليهود من آمن بالفضل الذي أوتيه الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم أو العرب على ما تقدم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sequence develops the rebuke of Jewish envy by adducing the honor given to their ancestors, showing they had no reason to begrudge others.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه تعالى لما أنكر على اليهود حسدهم الناس على فضل الله الذي آتاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage consoles Muhammad: Jews and their ancestors, even their prophets, were divided into believers and unbelievers, so division is expected around a prophet outside their lineage.
rows.anchor: وتضمنت هذه الآية تسلية الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم في كونهم يحسدونه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وابن جبير وعكرمة وابن يعمر والجحدري
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the doubled verb with ḍamma on ṣād in a passive form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وابن عباس، وابن جبير، وعكرمة، وابن يعمر، والجحدري: ومن صد عنه برفع الصاد مبنيا للمفعول.

rows.speaker: أبي وأبو الحوراء وأبو رجاء والحوقي
rows.claim: These readers use kasra on ṣād in the passive form; Abu Hayyan notes permissible passive vowel patterns for doubled triliteral verbs and the possibility of ishmaam.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي وأبو الحوراء وأبو رجاء والحوقي، بكسر الصاد مبنيا للمفعول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away is not a lexical opposite of belief; context means some believed and followed him while others rejected and turned away.
rows.anchor: والصد ليس مقابلا للإيمان إلا من حيث المعنى، وكان المعنى والله أعلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sa'ir means intense burning and kindling, an idiom for the severity of punishment awaiting those who turned away.
rows.anchor: وكفى بجهنم سعيرا أي احتراقا والتهابا أي لمن صد عنه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sa'ir is an accusative specification; the implied wording is “the blaze of Hell suffices as a blaze,” a figure for severe punishment.
rows.anchor: وسعيرا يميز وهو شدة توقد النار. والتقدير: وكفى بسعير جهنم سعيرا

words: إن الذين كفروا بآياتنا سوف نصليهم نارا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning the divided response and Hell for those who turn away, the passage describes disbelievers' punishment and then believers' reward, paralleling another verse's contrast.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر قوله: ومنهم من صد عنه، وكفى بجهنم سعيرا أتبع ذلك بما أعد الله للكافرين بآياته

rows.speaker: حميد
rows.claim: Hamid reads the verb from ṣ-l-y rather than the majority's form from aṣlā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور نصليهم من أصلى. وقرأ حميد: نصليهم من صليت.

rows.speaker: سلام ويعقوب
rows.claim: Sallam and Ya'qub read the pronoun suffix with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سلام ويعقوب: نصليهم بضم الهاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Every time” is an adverbial phrase added to temporal maṣdariyya mā and governed by “replace”; its clause carries conditional force, is circumstantial, and is governed by “make them enter.”
rows.anchor: انتصاب كل على الظرف لأنه مضاف إلى ما المصدرية الظرفية، والعامل فيه بدلناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replacement can change qualities while preserving an entity or replace the entity itself; the apparent sense is a new skin after the former one softens, withers, and disappears.
rows.anchor: والتبديل على معنيين: تبديل في الصفات مع بقاء العين، وتبديل في الذوات بأن تذهب العين

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says skins grow from flesh, so when a sinner's skin burns God replaces it with another skin made from that person's flesh.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: إن الجلود تخلق من اللحم، فإذا أحرق جلد بدله الله من لحم الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the same skins return after burning, as bodies are restored after decay in graves, so their qualities change but not their identity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي بعينها تعاد بعد إحراقها، كما تعاد الأجساد بعد البلى في القبور

rows.speaker: الفضيل
rows.claim: Al-Fudayl interprets the process as making what was cooked become uncooked again.
rows.anchor: وقال الفضيل: يجعل النضيج غير نضيج.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: One view says skins are replaced seven times each day; al-Hasan says seventy times.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تبدل كل يوم سبع مرات. وقال الحسن: سبعين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan calls far-fetched the view that the skins are tar garments mixed inseparably with bodies and replaced a hundred or even a hundred thousand times daily.
rows.anchor: وأبعد من ذهب إلى أن الجلود هي سرابيل من قطران تخالط جلودهم مخالطة لا يمكن إزالتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also rejects as far-fetched the metaphor that each apparent end of the torment begins anew, expressing its uninterrupted duration.
rows.anchor: وأبعد أيضا من ذهب إلى أن هذا استعارة عن الدوام، كلما انتهى فقد ابتدأ من أوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people of Hell are clothed in white skins like sheets of paper.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يلبسهم الله جلودا بيضاء كأنها قراطيس.

rows.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
rows.claim: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya says the people of Hell wear skins that feel pain although the skins themselves do not feel it.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى: يلبس أهل النار جلودا تؤلمهم ولا تؤلم هي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each new skin lets them taste pain again; “taste” suggests an initial painful sensation, preventing habituation.
rows.anchor: ليذوقوا العذاب أي ذلك التبديل كلما نضجت الجلود، هو ليذوقوا ألم العذاب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the phrase to mean punishment continues without interruption, like praying that someone remain in honor and increase in it.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ليذوقوا العذاب ليدوم لهم دونه ولا ينقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is invincible and cannot be overcome, and wise in placing things where they belong.
rows.anchor: إن الله كان عزيزا حكيما أي عزيزا لا يغالب، حكيما يضع الأشياء مواضعها.

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says nothing can prevent God from doing what He wills to criminals, and that His wisdom means He punishes only those who deserve it, justly.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري: عزيز لا يمتنع عليه شيء

words: كذلك يبين الله لكم آياته لعلكم تشكرون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding explanation makes God's signs, laws, and rulings clear so people may thank Him for teaching them and easing their way out of difficulty.
rows.anchor: كذلك أي مثل ذلك البيان يبين الله لكم آياته أعلام شريعته وأحكامه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion is Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas's quarrel: after emigrants and Helpers drank and boasted, an Ansari struck Sa'd with a camel jaw and split his nose.
rows.anchor: نزلت بسبب قصة سعد بن أبي وقاص حين شرب طائفة من الأنصار والمهاجرين فتفاخروا

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Another account connects the revelation to Umar's prayer for a clear explanation about wine.
rows.anchor: وقيل بسبب قول عمر اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account links the revelation to the lengthy incident in which Hamza hamstrung Ali's she-camel and taunted him.
rows.anchor: وقيل بسبب قصة حمزة وعلي حين عقر شارف علي وقال: هل أنتم إلا عبيد لأبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say prohibition came gradually, beginning with the ban on approaching prayer while drunk and culminating in this verse.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان أمر الخمر ونزول الآيات بتدريج، فنزل يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says an intoxicated Companion recited the disbelievers' sura inaccurately at Maghrib; drinking-related incidents then led to prohibition.
rows.anchor: وقيل بسبب قراءة بعض الصحابة وكان منتشيا في صلاة المغرب قل يا أيها الكافرون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says two Ansari clans became drunk and disorderly; when sober, each saw bruises and blamed the other, creating enmity that prompted the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزلت بسبب حيين من الأنصار ثملوا وعربدوا فلما صحوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse follows the order to consume lawful good provisions and not forbid lawful things without sin; it addresses wine and gambling, the pleasures people valued most.
rows.anchor: ومناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها أنه لما أمر تعالى بأكل ما رزقهم حلالا طيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People defended wine as relieving worry, energizing and emboldening drinkers, and prompting generosity, and gambling as increasing wealth and giving the pleasure of victory; the verse exposes the greater harms of those pleasures.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يقولون الخمر تطرد الهموم وتنشط النفس وتشجع الجبان وتبعث على المكارم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pre-Islamic poet praises a trusted brother for not wasting his wealth on wine, though his generosity can exhaust his money; Abu Hayyan uses the verse to note wine's ruinous cost.
rows.anchor: فقال: أخي ثقة لا تتلف الخمر ماله ... ولكنه قد يهلك المال نائله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine destroys reason and wealth and leads to murder, intense hatred, and sins, since reason restrains these evils; gambling takes wealth wrongfully.
rows.anchor: وتنشأ عنها مفاسد أخر من قتل النفس وشدة البغضاء وارتكاب المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to believers and the prohibited things were entrenched desires and habits; wine was not yet forbidden, with its prohibition following Uhud in 3 AH.
rows.anchor: وهذا الخطاب للمؤمنين والذي منعوا منه في هذه الآية هي شهوات وعادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan dates the prohibition of wine to after the Battle of Uhud in the third year after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: فأما الخمر فكانت لم تحرم بعد وإنما نزل تحريمها بعد وقعة أحد سنة ثلاث من الهجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ansab are sacrificial stones, calling them filth removes any lingering reverence among weak believers; if they are idols, the grouping emphasizes avoiding them like idols.
rows.anchor: وأما الأنصاب فإن كانت الحجارة التي يذبحون عندها وينحرون فحكم عليها بالرجس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The azlam were lots; most people used one marked “no” and another marked “yes.”
rows.anchor: وأما الأزلام التي كان الأكثرون يتخذونها في أحدها لا وفي الآخر

words: وإذا رأيت الذين يخوضون في آياتنا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command addresses the Prophet but includes believers, since the reason for the prohibition—listening to mockery of God's signs—applies to them too.
rows.anchor: هذا خطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ويدخل فيه المؤمنون لأن علة النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view restricts the command to the Prophet because his departure and anger troubled mockers in a way that believers' departure did not.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو خاص بتوحيده لأن قيامه عنهم كان يشق عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressee may instead be any listener; the mockers are variously identified as polytheists, Jews, or people of heterodox views.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خطاب للسامع والذين يخوضون المشركون أو اليهود أو أصحاب الأهواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes “saw” as visual perception with one object and an omitted state: seeing the mockers while engaged in mockery.
rows.anchor: ورأيت هنا بصرية ولذلك تعدت إلى واحد ولا بد من تقدير حال محذوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking “saw” as mental knowledge is remote: it requires omitting the second object of a verb of knowing, an omission some grammarians forbid and others consider rare.
rows.anchor: وقيل: رأيت علمية لأن الخوض في الآيات ليس مما يدرك بحاسة البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Wading” in God's signs is a metaphor for mocking and attacking them; Quraysh did this in their gatherings.
rows.anchor: والخوض في الآيات كناية عن الاستهزاء بها والطعن فيها. وكانت قريش في أنديتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away means not sitting with the mockers and leaving them; it is not merely inward disapproval.
rows.anchor: فأعرض عنهم أي لا تجالسهم وقم عنهم وليس إعراضا بالقلب وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators identify the quoted rule against sitting with people while God's signs are denied and mocked with this command; one may return once they change the subject.
rows.anchor: وقد نزل عليكم في الكتاب أن إذا سمعتم آيات الله يكفر بها ويستهزأ بها فلا تقعدوا معهم

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Hawfi says the pronoun refers to the mockery, as a poem shows a fool running toward foolishness when warned away from it.
rows.anchor: والضمير في غيره قال الحوفي عائد إلى الخوض كما قال الشاعر:

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa says the pronoun returns to the meaning of the signs, since they constitute talk or discourse.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: إنما ذكر الهاء لأنه أعادها على معنى الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Satan distracts the Prophet until he forgets the ban on sitting with mockers, he must not sit with them once reminded of the prohibition.
rows.anchor: أي إن شغلك بوسوسته حتى تنسى النهي عن مجالستهم فلا تقعد معهم بعد الذكرى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows that Satan caused forgetfulness before the ban was revealed, since reason itself rejects sitting with mockers; once reminded, one must leave.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يراد وإن كان الشيطان ينسيك قبل النهي قبح مجالسة المستهزئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says this reading conflicts with the apparent conditional sequence, since the command preceded the condition and both clauses describe future circumstances.
rows.anchor: وهو خلاف ظاهر الشرط لأنه قد نهي عن القعود معهم قبل ثم عطف على الشرط السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first condition uses “when” because mockery is certain, while the second uses “if” because forgetting is uncertain.
rows.anchor: وما أحسن مجيء الشرط الأول بإذا التي هي للمحقق لأن كونهم يخوضون في الآيات محقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them wrongdoers identifies the cause of their mockery: they transgress limits and put things in the wrong places.
rows.anchor: وجاء مع القوم الظالمين تنبيها على علة الخوض في الآيات والطعن فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya notes a conditional construction usually takes the emphatic nun but can omit it; the cited poetic example is cut off in the excerpt.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وأما شرط ويلزمها النون الثقيلة في الأغلب وقد لا تلزم كما قال الشاعر:
